state.task: Two agents analysed Java code for path traversal (CWE-22). Their final answers follow, then the code of each method in question.
agent_answers: {"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "ClassPathResource", "method": "getInputStream", "explanation": "The getInputStream method directly uses the path field, which originates from System.getenv() without any validation or sanitization, allowing untrusted path data to flow unchanged to the ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream() call, creating a path traversal vulnerability."}]}

{"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "ClassPathResource", "method": "ClassPathResource", "explanation": "The constructor accepts an attacker-controlled path (from an environment variable) and only applies StringUtils.cleanPath and removes a leading slash. It does not validate that the resulting path stays within an allowed resource root, nor does it perform any path traversal countermeasure beyond basic cleaning. This allows directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../') to remain in the path, which will later be used unsafely in getInputStream()."}, {"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "ClassPathResource", "method": "getInputStream", "explanation": "The getInputStream() method takes the stored path derived from untrusted input and passes it directly as the first argument to ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(String) (the static-taint SINK) without any containment check, allow-listing, or canonicalization against a base directory. Combined with the insufficient validation in the constructor, this allows an attacker to traverse out of the intended classpath root and read arbitrary files accessible to the classloader's filesystem roots."}]}
